Cyber Attack Disrupts Payment Systems Across Poland, Impacting Commerce

WARSAW, June 18 — A widespread cyber attack on Poland’s national electronic payments network has left businesses and consumers struggling to conduct transactions on Tuesday, with authorities scrambling to restore service and reassure the public as the disruption continues.

The attack, which began in the early hours of the morning, has targeted the core settlement infrastructure used by banks, retailers, and government agencies, according to the Ministry of Digital Affairs. The system, operated by the Warsaw-based PolPay Clearing House, processes the vast majority of electronic card and bank transfers nationwide.

“Initial analysis indicates a sophisticated and coordinated assault on our transaction processing systems,” said Deputy Minister for Digital Security Zofia Grabowska at a midday press conference. “Our teams are working around the clock to mitigate the impact and restore normal operations. We urge the public to remain patient as we address this unprecedented situation.”

Major supermarkets and petrol stations have reported long queues as point-of-sale terminals fail to process card payments. Small businesses, many of which rely on mobile payment apps, have been forced to accept cash only or temporarily close. The Polish Retailers Association estimates that sales volumes in affected outlets have dropped by as much as 60% since the morning.

“There’s a lot of confusion. Customers are frustrated, but we’re doing our best to keep everyone informed,” said Tomasz Nowak, manager of a FreshMart grocery store in Kraków. “We haven’t seen anything like this before.”

The Polish Banking Union said there was no evidence of customer funds being lost or compromised, but warned that interbank transfers and ATM withdrawals could be delayed until systems are fully restored.

Poland’s Financial Supervision Authority has convened an emergency meeting with payment providers and central bank officials. Authorities have not confirmed the source of the attack. Investigation is ongoing.
